uncited: It processes voxel face vectors (VFVs) to generate a closed, oriented surface composed of triangles (3-cycles).
Voxels are classified as "active" (value $\ge$ isovalue $T_f$) or "inactive" (value $< T_f$).
*   **Voxel Face Vector (VFV):** A directed vector connecting a boundary face center (support point) to a juncture (edge midpoint).
*   **Support Point:** The center of a voxel face separating an active and an inactive voxel.
*   **VESTA Cycle Vector:** A vector connecting two support points, formed by replacing connected VFV pairs.
*   **N-cycle:** A closed loop of VESTA cycle vectors.
*   **Connectivity Mode:** Determines handling of Points of Ambiguity (POAs).
*   *Disconnect:* Successor VFV belongs to the same voxel (left turn in 2D analog).
*   *Connect:* Successor VFV belongs to the other voxel (right turn in 2D analog).
*   *Mixed:* Mode determined locally by gray-level thresholds.
*   **Resolution Mode:** Determines N-cycle decomposition.
*   *Low (L):* No additional points; N-cycles decomposed by inserting antiparallel vector pairs.
*   *High (H):* Additional average point (center of mass of cycle vertices) inserted for decomposition.
**Identify Boundary Faces:** For every active voxel, check its 6 neighbors.
If a neighbor is inactive, record the shared face as a boundary face.
The center of this face is a support point.

**Define VFVs:** For each boundary face, define 4 VFVs connecting the face center to the 4 edge midpoints (junctures) in counterclockwise order relative to the range vector (from active voxel center to inactive neighbor center).
**Connect VFVs:** At each juncture, connect the origin of a VFV to the tip of a VFV from a neighboring boundary face.
This forms oriented paths between support points.
**Resolve Ambiguities (POAs):** A POA occurs when two active voxels share only a single edge (in 3D) or point (in 2D analog).
At a POA, 4 incoming and 4 outgoing VFVs exist.
Apply the chosen Connectivity Mode globally or locally to select the successor VFV.
**Form Cycles:** Replace connected VFV pairs with VESTA cycle vectors.
All cycles are confined to a $2 \times 2 \times 2$ voxel neighborhood.
*   In *Low* mode: Insert antiparallel vector pairs to break the N-cycle into 3-cycles, preserving orientation.
*   In *High* mode: Calculate the average point of all support points in the cycle.
Connect this average point to all vertices of the N-cycle to form triangles.
**Displace Support Points (Optional for Isosurfaces):** Move support points along their range vectors based on linear interpolation of field values to approximate the isosurface.
Recalculate average points for High mode if displaced.
DICONEX (DIlated CONtour EXtraction) is the 2D analog of VESTA.
It constructs gap-free contours from binary image data by connecting Initial Contour Vectors (ICVs) into closed cycles.
ICVs are oriented pixel edges separating active from inactive pixels, with the active pixel to the left.
At Points of Ambiguity (POAs) where active pixels touch at a single point, DICONEX uses a "disconnect" mode (left turn, same pixel) or "connect" mode (right turn, different pixel) to resolve gaps.
*   **Time Complexity:** Linear with respect to the number of active voxels and boundary faces.
The marching variant is more memory-efficient than the original global processing.
*   **Memory Complexity:** Original VESTA requires large memory to process the entire dataset at once.
Marching VESTA reduces this by processing $2 \times 2 \times 2$ neighborhoods.

*   **Performance:** In benchmarks with 241x81 images (8,000 active voxels), VESTA produced 6,406 triangles in ~0.124s, compared to MCA's 0.096s but with significantly more redundant points (19,218 vs 3,326).
Minimizes redundant support points compared to MCA.
High resolution mode adds computational overhead for average point calculation.
